title: Configuring a Java Project knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Configuring a Java Project” in the supplied Java curriculum?
options: Understanding source roots and output directories
questions.explanation: The supplied PDF lists “Creating a project directory” under lesson 17, “Configuring a Java Project”.

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with configuring a java project?
options: Make assumptions explicit, use a minimal example, and verify the result with a boundary or failure case.
Assume the first successful run proves the code is correct.
Change several unrelated parts until the output looks plausible.
Ignore runtime/version requirements if the code looks familiar.
questions.answer_key: Make assumptions explicit, use a minimal example, and verify the result with a boundary or failure case.
questions.explanation: Make assumptions explicit, use a minimal example, and verify the result with a boundary or failure case. A small reproducible test provides stronger evidence than assumption or trial-and-error changes.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest first step when checking an example related to configuring a java project?
options: Check both `java -version` and `javac -version`, then confirm the terminal is using the intended JDK.
Skip reproducing the behavior and change multiple settings at once.
Trust a screenshot without checking the program or version that produced it.
Disable all validation and error handling.
questions.answer_key: Check both `java -version` and `javac -version`, then confirm the terminal is using the intended JDK.
questions.explanation: Check both `java -version` and `javac -version`, then confirm the terminal is using the intended JDK. This approach makes the result repeatable and helps isolate the cause of a mismatch.
